patient_profile.history: Acute inferior wall myocardial infarction 36 hours ago, hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus

assessment.cardiovascular: New harsh holosystolic murmur at left lower sternal border, JVD to 10 cm H2O, cool extremities
assessment.respiratory: Bibasilar crackles halfway up lung fields

diagnostic_results.findings: Sinus tachycardia with Q waves and resolving ST elevations in II, III, aVF

questions.stem: Based on the sudden change in the patient's clinical presentation, which action should the nurse take first?

options.text: Administer the scheduled dose of metoprolol tartrate to reduce myocardial oxygen demand
Hold the metoprolol and immediately notify the provider of a suspected mechanical complication
Place the patient in modified Trendelenburg position and initiate a 1,000 mL normal saline bolus
Obtain a stat portable chest radiograph and schedule a routine transthoracic echocardiogram

rationales.correct: A new harsh holosystolic murmur 36 hours post-MI accompanied by acute cardiogenic shock (hypotension, tachycardia, pulmonary crackles, elevated lactate) indicates papillary muscle rupture or ventricular septal rupture. Beta-blockers are strictly contraindicated in acute cardiogenic shock and decompensated pulmonary edema due to negative inotropic effects. Immediate provider notification for emergent echocardiography and surgical evaluation is required.

incorrect.rationale: Metoprolol will further depress myocardial contractility and heart rate, worsening cardiogenic shock.
Rapid crystalloid loading in acute pulmonary edema with elevated JVD will exacerbate respiratory failure.
Waiting for a routine echocardiogram delays life-saving emergent intervention.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes cues of mechanical post-MI rupture and cardiogenic shock, withholds a contraindicated beta-blocker, and escalates emergently.

patient_profile.history: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease), admitted with acute viral gastroenteritis

assessment.gastrointestinal: Persistent nausea, vomiting, diffuse abdominal tenderness
assessment.integumentary: Hyperpigmentation of palmar creases, poor skin turgor

questions.stem: The nurse identifies that the patient is experiencing an adrenal crisis. Which intervention is the highest priority?

options.text: Initiate a rapid IV infusion of 0.9% sodium chloride and administer hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg IV
Administer sodium polystyrene sulfonate 30 g PO to correct serum hyperkalemia
Initiate an IV infusion of 0.45% sodium chloride with 20 mEq potassium chloride
Administer oral fludrocortisone 0.1 mg and prednisone 20 mg with a small sip of water

rationales.correct: Adrenal crisis is a life-threatening emergency characterized by refractory hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and hypoglycemia. Immediate restoration of intravascular volume with isotonic 0.9% sodium chloride (plus dextrose for hypoglycemia) and high-dose IV glucocorticoid replacement (hydrocortisone 100 mg IV) are the top priorities.

incorrect.rationale: Oral medications are unsafe in a lethargic, vomiting patient, and restoring volume plus hydrocortisone will shift and excrete potassium.
Hypotonic saline worsens hyponatremia and hypotension, and potassium is strictly contraindicated given serum potassium of 6.1 mEq/L.
Oral steroids are inappropriate during acute emesis, lethargy, and shock; parenteral administration is required.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies acute adrenal crisis from classic triad of shock, electrolyte derangement, and hypoglycemia, prioritizing IV volume and glucocorticoid rescue.

patient_profile.history: Subarachnoid hemorrhage status post aneurysm clipping 4 days ago

assessment.neurological: New onset left-sided pronator drift and mild dysarthria; pupils 3 mm and briskly reactive bilaterally

diagnostic_results.findings: Elevated mean flow velocity in the right middle cerebral artery (185 cm/s)

questions.stem: Which nursing action is most appropriate to prevent permanent ischemic neurological injury in this patient?

options.text: Administer nimodipine 60 mg as scheduled and prepare to initiate induced hypertension per protocol
Administer IV labetalol 10 mg to lower systolic blood pressure below 120 mmHg
Elevate the head of the bed to 60 degrees and restrict IV fluid intake to 50 mL/hr
Administer mannitol 1 g/kg IV bolus to induce osmotic diuresis

rationales.correct: Cerebral vasospasm typically peaks 4 to 14 days after subarachnoid hemorrhage, causing delayed cerebral ischemia (new pronator drift, dysarthria, high TCD velocities). Nimodipine prevents ischemic deficits from vasospasm, and maintaining euvolemia with induced hypertension (elevating cerebral perfusion pressure) improves blood flow past spastic vessels once the aneurysm is secured.

incorrect.rationale: Lowering blood pressure in a patient with a secured aneurysm and active vasospasm reduces cerebral perfusion pressure and worsens stroke.
Fluid restriction causes hypovolemia, which severely exacerbates cerebral ischemia during vasospasm.
Mannitol induces intravascular volume depletion and is not indicated for vasospasm without elevated ICP herniation.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Differentiates post-SAH cerebral vasospasm from rebleeding and selects hemodynamic augmentation and calcium channel blockade.

patient_profile.history: Severe persistent asthma, admitted with acute asthma exacerbation

assessment.respiratory: Initially had loud expiratory wheezing; now lung sounds are markedly diminished with a silent chest and intercostal retractions

questions.stem: How should the nurse interpret the disappearance of wheezing alongside a PaCO2 of 48 mmHg?

options.text: Bronchospasm is resolving in response to nebulized bronchodilators
Impending respiratory arrest due to critical airway obstruction and ventilatory muscle fatigue
Expected respiratory compensation for mild metabolic acidosis
Development of a spontaneous tension pneumothorax requiring immediate needle decompression

rationales.correct: In acute severe asthma, patients initially hyperventilate and have hypocapnia (low PaCO2). Normalization or elevation of PaCO2 (48 mmHg) paired with a 'silent chest' indicates airflow is so severely restricted that wheezes can no longer be generated, signaling impending respiratory arrest requiring immediate intubation.

incorrect.rationale: Resolution of bronchospasm would be accompanied by improved SpO2, reduced respiratory rate, and normalized PaCO2, not hypoxemia and acidosis.
Compensation for metabolic acidosis lowers PaCO2 via hyperventilation, whereas here PaCO2 is elevated causing respiratory acidosis.
Bilateral diminished breath sounds with rising PaCO2 in status asthmaticus reflects global airway obstruction rather than unilateral tension pneumothorax.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Interprets the ominous clinical transition from wheezing/hypocapnia to silent chest/hypercapnia as impending ventilatory failure.

patient_profile.history: End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis via left brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula

assessment.neurological: Restless, complaining of throbbing headache during the final 30 minutes of hemodialysis
assessment.cardiovascular: No peripheral edema

questions.stem: The patient suddenly develops nausea, blurred vision, and confusion. Which action should the hemodialysis nurse take first?

options.text: Slow or stop the hemodialysis blood flow rate and notify the nephrologist immediately
Increase the ultrafiltration rate to remove excess cerebral fluid rapidly
Administer acetaminophen 650 mg PO and reassess neurological status in 30 minutes
Place the patient flat in supine position and infuse 500 mL of 0.9% sodium chloride

rationales.correct: The patient is exhibiting dialysis disequilibrium syndrome (DDS), caused by rapid removal of urea from the blood faster than it can diffuse out of brain cells, creating an osmotic gradient that shifts water into the brain and causes cerebral edema. Stopping or slowing dialysis immediately halts further osmotic shift and prevents seizures or coma.

incorrect.rationale: Increasing ultrafiltration removes intravascular volume, risking hypotension without reducing intracellular cerebral edema.
Delaying intervention while treating headache symptomatically risks progression to seizures and brainstem herniation.
Placing the patient flat increases intracranial pressure, and the patient is hypertensive (168/94 mmHg), not hypovolemic.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes dialysis disequilibrium syndrome in a patient with high pre-dialysis BUN and halts the dialysis osmotic gradient immediately.

patient_profile.history: Closed comminuted right tibial shaft fracture reduced and immobilized in a long-leg plaster cast 6 hours ago

assessment.musculoskeletal: Reports 9/10 deep throbbing pain in right lower leg unrelieved by IV morphine 4 mg given 30 minutes ago; severe pain elicited with passive dorsiflexion of the right great toe; toes are warm with capillary refill of 2 seconds

questions.stem: What is the nurse's priority action based on these assessment findings?

options.text: Elevate the right leg above the level of the heart on two pillows and apply ice packs
Notify the orthopedic surgeon immediately to bivalve the cast and evaluate for compartment syndrome
Reassure the patient that normal capillary refill rules out neurovascular compromise
Administer an additional dose of IV morphine 4 mg and reassess in 1 hour

rationales.correct: Pain out of proportion to the injury, refractory to opioids, and exacerbated by passive stretching of muscles in the compartment are the earliest hallmark signs of acute compartment syndrome. Pulselessness and delayed capillary refill are late signs indicating irreversible necrosis. Immediate provider notification to bivalve/split the cast and measure compartment pressures is critical.

incorrect.rationale: Elevating an extremity above heart level in suspected compartment syndrome decreases arterial perfusion pressure and worsens tissue ischemia; keep at heart level.
Normal pulses and capillary refill do not exclude compartment syndrome because intracompartmental pressure compromises capillary microcirculation long before occluding major arteries.
Masking pain with additional opioids without relieving external compression delays fasciotomy and risks limb loss.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies early acute compartment syndrome despite intact distal perfusion and initiates immediate mechanical decompression.

patient_profile.history: G3P2 at 39 weeks gestation in active labor; artificial rupture of membranes performed 2 minutes ago

assessment.obstetric: Fetal heart rate baseline dropped abruptly from 140 bpm to 75 bpm with prolonged deceleration; on sterile vaginal exam, the nurse palpates a pulsating loop of umbilical cord in the vagina

questions.stem: While calling for emergency assistance, which immediate action must the nurse perform?

options.text: Insert two sterile gloved fingers into the vagina to lift the fetal presenting part off the umbilical cord
Gently push the prolapsed umbilical cord back into the uterine cavity above the cervix
Place the patient in high-Fowler's position to use gravity to facilitate rapid vaginal delivery
Increase the IV oxytocin infusion rate to accelerate cervical dilation

rationales.correct: Overt umbilical cord prolapse is an obstetric emergency where the fetal presenting part compresses the cord against the pelvic brim, causing acute fetal hypoxia. The nurse must keep a sterile gloved hand in the vagina applying continuous upward pressure against the presenting part until emergent cesarean delivery is performed, while placing the mother in knee-chest or steep Trendelenburg position.

incorrect.rationale: Never attempt to push a prolapsed cord back into the uterus, as this causes severe umbilical vasospasm and worsens fetal hypoxia.
High-Fowler's position increases downward fetal pressure on the cord; knee-chest or Trendelenburg is required.
Oxytocin stimulates contractions that further compress the cord and must be stopped immediately.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Executes immediate manual elevation of the fetal presenting part to relieve umbilical cord compression during an acute prolapse.

patient_profile.history: Unimmunized child brought to ED by parents with sudden onset high fever and severe sore throat over 4 hours

assessment.respiratory: Sitting upright leaning forward with chin thrust out, drooling continuously, muffled 'hot potato' voice, inspiratory stridor, no cough

questions.stem: Which action by the nurse is contraindicated and could precipitate complete airway obstruction?

options.text: Inspecting the posterior pharynx using a tongue depressor and penlight
Allowing the child to remain sitting upright in the parent's lap
Administering humidified blow-by oxygen without agitating the child
Notifying pediatric anesthesia and otolaryngology for emergent airway preparation

rationales.correct: The child presents with classic acute epiglottitis (tripod position, drooling, dysphagia, dysphonia, high fever, absence of cough). Visualizing the throat with a tongue depressor or obtaining throat cultures can trigger violent laryngospasm and complete, fatal airway occlusion.

incorrect.rationale: Keeping the child calm and upright in the parent's lap prevents agitation and maintains airway patency.
Non-threatening humidified blow-by oxygen improves oxygenation without causing crying or laryngospasm.
Emergent airway team preparation for controlled intubation in the operating room is essential.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies acute epiglottitis and avoids pharyngeal stimulation that triggers fatal laryngospasm.

patient_profile.history: Atrial fibrillation, heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease stage 3

assessment.gastrointestinal: Anorexia and nausea for 2 days
assessment.visual: Reports seeing yellow-green halos around the room lights

diagnostic_results.findings: Junctional bradycardia with frequent premature ventricular contractions

questions.stem: Which pathophysiological relationship explains why this patient developed digoxin toxicity?

options.text: Furosemide-induced hypokalemia increases digoxin binding to myocardial Na+/K+-ATPase pumps
Atrial fibrillation accelerates hepatic metabolism of digoxin into active toxic metabolites
Hypokalemia competes with digoxin at renal tubular secretion sites, raising serum levels
Furosemide directly inhibits gastrointestinal absorption of digoxin, causing rebound toxicity

rationales.correct: Digoxin and potassium compete for the same binding site on the cardiac Na+/K+-ATPase pump. Loop diuretic (furosemide)-induced hypokalemia reduces extracellular potassium, allowing excessive digoxin binding and precipitating toxicity (bradycardia, xanthopsia/yellow-green halos, nausea, PVCs), compounded by reduced renal clearance in CKD.

incorrect.rationale: Digoxin is primarily excreted unchanged by the kidneys, not extensively metabolized by the liver.
Hypokalemia potentiates digoxin's effect at the myocardial receptor site rather than blocking tubular secretion.
Furosemide does not inhibit digoxin absorption or cause rebound toxicity.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Connects loop-diuretic hypokalemia and renal impairment to digoxin toxicity manifestations.

patient_profile.history: Schizophrenia started on haloperidol 10 mg PO twice daily 3 days ago

assessment.neurological: Mute, stuporous, generalized 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, diaphoretic

questions.stem: The nurse recognizes this clinical presentation as neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS). Which provider order should the nurse anticipate implementing first?

options.text: Discontinue haloperidol immediately and initiate aggressive IV hydration and external cooling
Administer benztropine 2 mg IM to relieve acute extrapyramidal muscle rigidity
Administer cyproheptadine 12 mg PO to block central serotonin receptors
Increase haloperidol dosage to treat worsening catatonic stupor

rationales.correct: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a life-threatening idiosyncratic reaction to dopamine antagonists (haloperidol) characterized by hyperthermia (40.2°C), lead-pipe rigidity, autonomic instability, altered mental status, and rhabdomyolysis (CK 14,800 U/L). Immediate discontinuation of the antipsychotic, aggressive IV fluid resuscitation to prevent acute kidney injury from myoglobinuria, and cooling are paramount, alongside dantrolene or bromocriptine.

incorrect.rationale: Anticholinergics like benztropine impair sweating and thermoregulation, worsening life-threatening hyperthermia in NMS.
Cyproheptadine is used for serotonin syndrome (which presents with hyperreflexia and clonus), not NMS (which presents with lead-pipe rigidity and hyporeflexia).
Continuing or increasing haloperidol is fatal in NMS.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Distinguishes neuroleptic malignant syndrome from serotonin syndrome and catatonia, prioritizing antipsychotic cessation and organ protection.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative total hip arthroplasty with symptomatic anemia (Hgb 6.8 g/dL)

assessment.general: 10 minutes after starting a unit of packed red blood cells, patient reports chills, severe lower back pain, and a feeling of impending doom
assessment.integumentary: Flushed skin, oozing at IV insertion site

questions.stem: What is the very first action the nurse must take?

options.text: Stop the blood transfusion immediately and disconnect the blood tubing from the IV catheter
Slow the transfusion rate to 10 mL/hr and administer diphenhydramine 25 mg IV
Flush the existing blood tubing with 0.9% sodium chloride to clear the line
Obtain a urine specimen to test for hemoglobinuria before stopping the infusion

rationales.correct: Chills, fever, severe lumbar/flank pain, hypotension, and oozing (early DIC) within minutes of starting a transfusion indicate an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction due to ABO incompatibility. Stopping the transfusion immediately limits the volume of incompatible blood infused; new saline tubing must then be attached directly to the IV hub to maintain vascular access.

incorrect.rationale: Continuing an incompatible transfusion at any rate can be fatal, and diphenhydramine only treats mild allergic urticaria.
Flushing the existing blood tubing pushes the remaining incompatible blood inside the tubing directly into the patient's bloodstream.
Stopping the infusion always precedes diagnostic specimen collection.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes acute hemolytic transfusion reaction and halts exposure immediately without flushing residual blood in the tubing.

patient_profile.history: Medical-surgical nursing team consisting of one RN, one LPN/LVN, and one assistive personnel (AP)

questions.stem: Which task is most appropriate for the registered nurse (RN) to delegate to the licensed practical/vocational nurse (LPN/LVN)?

options.text: Administering scheduled subcutaneous enoxaparin to a stable postoperative patient
Completing the initial admission nursing assessment for a patient transferred from the emergency department
Administering an IV push dose of furosemide 40 mg to a patient with acute pulmonary edema
Developing the discharge teaching plan for a newly diagnosed type 1 diabetic patient

rationales.correct: Administering a routine subcutaneous medication to a stable client with predictable outcomes may be appropriate for an LPN/LVN when permitted by the jurisdiction's nurse practice act, facility policy, the nurse's demonstrated competency, and the client's plan of care. The RN retains responsibility for initial assessment, care planning, teaching that requires RN judgment, and evaluation.

incorrect.rationale: Initial admission assessments require RN clinical judgment and cannot be delegated.
IV push medications to unstable patients (acute pulmonary edema) require RN administration and monitoring.
Developing initial comprehensive patient education plans is an RN responsibility; LPNs may reinforce established teaching.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Applies the Five Rights of Delegation to match task complexity and patient stability with LPN scope of practice.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with night sweats, 10-kg weight loss, hemoptysis, and cavitary right upper lobe lesion on chest radiograph

assessment.respiratory: Productive cough with blood-streaked sputum

questions.stem: Which infection control precaution is mandatory when caring for this patient?

options.text: Place the patient in an airborne infection isolation room (AIIR) and wear a fit-tested N95 respirator
Place the patient in a standard private room and wear a surgical mask within 3 feet
Place the patient on contact precautions with gown and gloves, keeping the door open for ventilation
Cohort the patient with another patient receiving treatment for bacterial pneumonia

rationales.correct: Active pulmonary tuberculosis is transmitted via airborne droplet nuclei (<5 microns) that remain suspended in air. An airborne infection isolation room (negative pressure with 6-12 air changes/hour) and a fit-tested N95 or PAPR respirator are mandatory.

incorrect.rationale: Standard surgical masks do not filter airborne droplet nuclei, and standard rooms lack negative-pressure exhaust.
Keeping the door open allows contaminated airborne nuclei to escape into the hallway.
Patients with active TB must never be cohorted with non-TB patients.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Selects airborne isolation and respiratory protection appropriate for Mycobacterium tuberculosis transmission.

patient_profile.history: Decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis with portal hypertension and esophageal varices

assessment.neurological: Drowsy, disoriented to time, exhibits asterixis (flapping tremor) when wrists are hyperextended
assessment.gastrointestinal: Moderate ascites, fetor hepaticus

questions.stem: Which finding indicates that the prescribed lactulose therapy is achieving its therapeutic goal?

options.text: The patient has 2 to 3 soft bowel movements per day and demonstrates improved orientation
The patient experiences 6 to 8 watery stools per day with decreased abdominal girth
The patient's serum ammonia level increases as ammonia is mobilized from tissue
The patient's urine output increases to greater than 60 mL/hr

rationales.correct: Lactulose acidifies the colonic lumen, trapping ammonia (NH3) as non-absorbable ammonium (NH4+) and promoting its fecal excretion. The therapeutic target is 2 to 3 soft stools daily accompanied by resolution of hepatic encephalopathy (improved mental status, resolution of asterixis).

incorrect.rationale: Excessive watery diarrhea (6-8 stools/day) causes dehydration, hypernatremia, and hypokalemia, which actually worsen hepatic encephalopathy.
Therapeutic lactulose lowers, rather than increases, serum ammonia levels.
Lactulose is a non-absorbable disaccharide laxative, not a diuretic.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Evaluates therapeutic efficacy vs. over-diuresis/dehydration risk during lactulose titration for hepatic encephalopathy.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative total thyroidectomy 18 hours ago

assessment.neurological: Complains of perioral numbness and tingling in fingertips; carpal spasm induced when blood pressure cuff is inflated above systolic pressure for 2 minutes

questions.stem: Which complication is the patient at highest immediate risk for developing if untreated?

options.text: Laryngospasm and acute airway obstruction
Thyroid storm with severe hyperpyrexia
Flaccid paralysis of the diaphragm
Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

rationales.correct: Inadvertent trauma or removal of the parathyroid glands during thyroidectomy causes acute hypoparathyroidism and severe hypocalcemia (positive Trousseau sign, paresthesias, prolonged QT). Severe hypocalcemia increases neuromuscular excitability, risking acute laryngospasm, stridor, and airway occlusion; IV calcium gluconate and emergency airway equipment must be immediately available.

incorrect.rationale: Thyroid storm presents with severe tachycardia, hyperthermia, and agitation, whereas these cues indicate acute hypocalcemic tetany.
Hypocalcemia causes neuromuscular hyperexcitability (tetany, spasms), whereas hypercalcemia or severe hypokalemia causes flaccid weakness.
Chronic hypercalcemia, not acute hypocalcemia, causes nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes Trousseau sign and paresthesias post-thyroidectomy as acute hypocalcemia carrying an immediate risk of laryngospasm.

patient_profile.history: G2P1 at 34 weeks gestation admitted with severe preeclampsia

assessment.neurological: Somnolent, patellar deep tendon reflexes absent (0+)
assessment.respiratory: Shallow respirations
assessment.genitourinary: Urine output 18 mL/hr over past 2 hours

questions.stem: Which actions should the nurse implement immediately? Select all that apply.

options.text: Discontinue the continuous intravenous magnesium sulfate infusion immediately
Administer calcium gluconate 1 g IV slowly over 3 minutes
Apply supplemental oxygen via nonrebreather mask and prepare for airway support
Administer furosemide 20 mg IV push to increase renal magnesium excretion
Place the patient in a left lateral recumbent position and initiate continuous ECG monitoring
Increase maintenance IV fluid infusion to 250 mL/hr to flush excess magnesium

rationales.correct: Oliguria (18 mL/hr) impaired renal clearance of magnesium sulfate, causing toxicity (Mg 9.4 mg/dL, RR 10/min, absent DTRs). Stopping the infusion (A), administering calcium gluconate (B), applying oxygen (C), and left lateral positioning with ECG monitoring (E) are immediate life-saving interventions.

incorrect.rationale: Loop diuretics require an order and worsen uteroplacental perfusion in preeclampsia.
Fluid boluses in oliguric preeclampsia risk acute pulmonary edema.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Synthesizes oliguria, bradypnea, and areflexia as magnesium toxicity and initiates immediate reversal.

patient_profile.history: Type 1 diabetes mellitus admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)

assessment.respiratory: Kussmaul respirations with fruity breath odor

questions.stem: Before initiating the continuous regular insulin infusion, which actions must the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hold the regular insulin infusion and notify the provider of the serum potassium level of 3.2 mEq/L
Begin the 0.9% sodium chloride IV fluid resuscitation bolus immediately
Verify adequate urine output before administering prescribed IV potassium replacement
Administer IV sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq push to rapidly normalize arterial pH
Establish continuous cardiac telemetry monitoring
Administer insulin glargine 20 units subcutaneously while waiting for potassium repletion

rationales.correct: Insulin drives extracellular potassium into cells. Initiating IV insulin when serum potassium is <3.3 mEq/L (here 3.2 mEq/L) can trigger fatal hypokalemic cardiac dysrhythmias. The nurse must start isotonic IV fluid resuscitation (B), hold insulin and request IV potassium replacement (A), confirm urine output before giving potassium (C), and place the patient on cardiac telemetry (E).

incorrect.rationale: Routine sodium bicarbonate is not indicated for pH >6.9 in DKA and causes paradoxical CNS acidosis and worsening hypokalemia.
Subcutaneous insulin also lowers serum potassium and is contraindicated until potassium is >=3.3 mEq/L.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Prevents insulin-induced fatal hypokalemia by holding insulin until serum potassium is corrected above 3.3 mEq/L.

patient_profile.history: Nursing home resident admitted from ED with urosepsis

questions.stem: Which interventions belong in the Surviving Sepsis Campaign Hour-1 Bundle for this patient? Select all that apply.

options.text: Obtain two sets of blood cultures prior to administering broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
Administer broad-spectrum intravenous antimicrobials within 1 hour
Infuse at least 30 mL/kg of IV crystalloid fluid for hypotension and lactate >=4 mmol/L
Initiate norepinephrine infusion if hypotension persists during or after fluid resuscitation
Delay antibiotic administration until urine and blood culture sensitivities return in 48 hours
Administer 5% albumin as the sole initial resuscitation fluid instead of crystalloids

rationales.correct: The Hour-1 Sepsis Bundle mandates measuring lactate, obtaining blood cultures prior to antimicrobials without delaying therapy (A), administering broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 hour (B), infusing 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid for hypotension or lactate >=4 mmol/L (C), and starting vasopressors (norepinephrine first-line) to maintain MAP >=65 mmHg if fluid-refractory (D).

incorrect.rationale: Each hour delay in effective antimicrobial administration in septic shock significantly increases mortality.
Balanced crystalloids or 0.9% saline are recommended as first-line resuscitation fluids, not albumin.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Applies evidence-based Hour-1 Sepsis Bundle interventions for septic shock.

patient_profile.history: Short bowel syndrome receiving continuous Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN) via right subclavian central venous catheter

assessment.general: Infusion pump alarms 'Occlusion/Empty'; nurse notes the TPN bag is empty and the pharmacy delivery is delayed by 45 minutes

questions.stem: Which nursing actions are appropriate when managing TPN therapy and this temporary delay? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hang a temporary infusion of 10% dextrose in water (D10W) at the same infusion rate as the TPN
Monitor point-of-care capillary blood glucose every 4 to 6 hours
Replace the TPN administration tubing and 0.22-micron filter every 24 hours
Infuse 0.9% sodium chloride through the TPN lumen until the new TPN bag arrives
Administer IV push potassium chloride through the dedicated TPN lumen
Increase the new TPN infusion rate by 25% once it arrives to catch up on missed calories

rationales.correct: Abrupt interruption of hypertonic dextrose TPN while endogenous insulin levels remain high precipitates severe rebound hypoglycemia; hanging D10W at the same rate prevents this (A). Regular capillary glucose checks (B) and changing TPN tubing/filters every 24 hours to prevent catheter-related bloodstream infection (C) are standard safety protocols.

incorrect.rationale: 0.9% sodium chloride contains no dextrose and will not prevent rebound hypoglycemia.
The TPN lumen must remain dedicated to prevent incompatibilities and infection.
Never accelerate TPN infusion rates to catch up, as this causes severe hyperglycemia and osmotic diuresis.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Prevents rebound hypoglycemia and line sepsis in TPN management.

patient_profile.history: Major depressive disorder admitted after an intentional acetaminophen overdose

assessment.psychiatric: Previously withdrawn and tearful for 3 days; today appears unusually calm, cheerful, and gives away her favorite books to another patient

questions.stem: Which nursing interventions are essential based on this sudden behavioral shift? Select all that apply.

options.text: Initiate continuous 1:1 visual observation immediately
Ask the patient directly if she is having thoughts or a plan to end her life
Conduct an environmental safety sweep of the patient's room and belongings
Recommend downgrading suicide precautions since her mood has markedly improved
Ensure oral medications are swallowed completely using a mouth check
Grant an unescorted pass to the hospital courtyard to reinforce positive coping

rationales.correct: A sudden unexplained shift from severe depression to serenity accompanied by giving away prized possessions is a classic warning sign that the patient has resolved to die by suicide and has formulated a lethal plan. Immediate 1:1 observation (A), direct suicide risk assessment (B), room contraband search (C), and cheeking/mouth checks (E) are required.

incorrect.rationale: Sudden calmness in a depressed inpatient signals peak suicide risk, not recovery.
Unescorted passes are strictly unsafe during acute suicidal ideation.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies covert suicidal behavioral cues (sudden euphoria, giving away belongings) and enforces maximum safety.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) receiving continuous unfractionated heparin infusion for new-onset atrial fibrillation

assessment.integumentary: Erythematous, painful necrotic skin plaque at previous subcutaneous heparin injection site; cool, pale left foot with diminished dorsalis pedis pulse

questions.stem: The nurse suspects Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT). Which actions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Discontinue all heparin products immediately, including heparin catheter flushes
Notify the provider and prepare to initiate a non-heparin anticoagulant such as argatroban
Send blood samples for heparin-PF4 antibody and serotonin release assays
Switch the patient to subcutaneous enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 hours
Initiate warfarin 10 mg PO immediately to replace heparin anticoagulation
Transfuse 2 units of platelets prophylactically for a platelet count below 70,000/mm³

rationales.correct: HIT is an immune-mediated prothrombotic disorder characterized by a >50% platelet drop 5-10 days after heparin exposure and paradoxical arterial/venous thrombosis (cool pale foot). All heparin sources must be stopped immediately (A), a direct thrombin inhibitor like argatroban must be started to prevent catastrophic thrombosis (B), and HIT antibody testing ordered (C).

incorrect.rationale: Low-molecular-weight heparins (enoxaparin) cross-react with HIT antibodies and are strictly contraindicated.
Warfarin must never be started during acute HIT until platelets recover (>150,000/mm³) because warfarin depletes protein C first, causing venous limb gangrene.
Prophylactic platelet transfusions fuel further thrombosis in HIT and are avoided unless life-threatening bleeding occurs.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies paradoxical prothrombotic HIT and prevents contraindicated LMWH, warfarin, and platelet administration.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with suspected Kawasaki disease on day 6 of persistent high fever

assessment.integumentary: Polymorphous maculopapular rash, erythema and edema of hands and feet
assessment.heent: Bilateral non-exudative conjunctival injection, strawberry tongue, cracked red lips, unilateral cervical lymphadenopathy

questions.stem: Which treatments and nursing interventions are indicated in the acute phase of Kawasaki disease? Select all that apply.

options.text: Administer high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg as a single infusion
Administer high-dose oral aspirin as prescribed for anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet effects
Prepare the child for a baseline transthoracic echocardiogram to evaluate coronary arteries
Monitor closely for signs of heart failure and fluid overload during IVIG infusion
Administer live MMR and varicella vaccines prior to hospital discharge
Substitute ibuprofen for aspirin to avoid any risk of Reye syndrome during therapy

rationales.correct: Kawasaki disease causes systemic medium-vessel vasculitis with a high risk of coronary artery aneurysms. Standard acute therapy is IVIG 2 g/kg (A) plus high-dose aspirin (B) initiated within 10 days of fever onset, alongside echocardiographic coronary surveillance (C) and monitoring for IVIG-induced volume overload/myocarditis (D).

incorrect.rationale: High-dose IVIG interferes with the immune response to live vaccines; MMR and varicella vaccines must be deferred for 11 months after IVIG.
Kawasaki disease is one of the few pediatric indications where aspirin is required; ibuprofen antagonizes aspirin's antiplatelet effect.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Selects evidence-based coronary aneurysm prevention and IVIG safety precautions in Kawasaki disease.

patient_profile.history: Rescued from an enclosed house fire 45 minutes ago; sustained deep partial- and full-thickness burns to face, neck, anterior chest, and bilateral arms (38% TBSA)

assessment.respiratory: Singed nasal hairs, carbonaceous sputum, hoarse voice, mild expiratory wheezing

questions.stem: Which priority nursing interventions are required during the emergent resuscitation phase? Select all that apply.

options.text: Prepare equipment for immediate prophylactic endotracheal intubation
Maintain 100% FiO2 humidified oxygen therapy to accelerate carbon monoxide elimination
Insert two large-bore IV catheters and initiate warmed Lactated Ringer's per fluid resuscitation formula
Titrate IV fluid infusion rate primarily to maintain adult urine output of 0.5 to 1 mL/kg/hr
Wean supplemental oxygen to 2 L/min nasal cannula because SpO2 reads 95%
Administer intramuscular morphine sulfate 10 mg into unburned deltoid tissue for pain

rationales.correct: Facial/neck burns, singed nasal hairs, carbonaceous sputum, and hoarseness indicate thermal inhalation injury; massive airway edema develops rapidly, mandating early prophylactic intubation (A). High-flow 100% oxygen shortens the half-life of carboxyhemoglobin from 4-6 hours to 40-60 minutes (B). Large-bore IV access with warmed Lactated Ringer's (C) titrated to urine output of 0.5-1 mL/kg/hr (D) prevents burn shock.

incorrect.rationale: Standard pulse oximetry cannot distinguish carboxyhemoglobin from oxyhemoglobin, producing falsely reassuring SpO2 readings.
IM analgesia is erratic and poorly absorbed due to third-spacing and hypoperfusion in burn shock; use IV opioids.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Prioritizes early airway control, carbon monoxide washout, and titrated fluid resuscitation in major thermal/inhalation burns.

patient_profile.history: Scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 1 hour

assessment.general: Patient states to the preoperative nurse, 'I signed the consent form last night, but I still don't understand why they might have to make a big open incision or what the risks are'

medications.name: Midazolam
medications.details: Ordered on call to OR; not yet given

questions.stem: Which actions must the nurse take in this situation? Select all that apply.

options.text: Withhold preoperative sedative medications such as midazolam
Notify the operating surgeon immediately so the surgeon can re-explain the procedure and risks
Document the patient's questions and notification of the surgeon in the medical record
Explain the surgical risks and conversion criteria in detail to obtain a new valid signature
Proceed with transport to the operating room because a signed consent form is already on the chart

rationales.correct: Informed consent requires true patient comprehension, not merely a signature. When a patient expresses uncertainty about procedural risks or alternatives, the nurse acts as an advocate by withholding sedatives that impair decision-making capacity (A), notifying the surgeon to provide required medical disclosure (B), and documenting the event (C).

incorrect.rationale: Explaining surgical risks, benefits, and alternatives is the legal responsibility of the provider performing the procedure, not the nurse.
Proceeding with surgery without informed comprehension violates patient autonomy and legal standards.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Upholds legal and ethical standards of informed consent by halting sedation and engaging the surgeon.

patient_profile.history: Ischemic stroke with dysphagia receiving continuous enteral nutrition via nasogastric tube

assessment.respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally
assessment.gastrointestinal: Soft, non-distended abdomen with active bowel sounds

questions.stem: Which nursing interventions reduce the risk of aspiration and tube complications during continuous enteral feeding? Select all that apply.

options.text: Maintain the head of the bed elevated at 30 to 45 degrees at all times during feeding
Verify initial tube placement via radiographic confirmation prior to starting first feeding
Flush the feeding tube with 30 mL of water every 4 hours and before/after medications
Check the external tube exit marking at the nares every shift to detect migration
Confirm ongoing tube placement before each shift by auscultating air insufflation over the epigastrium
Crush extended-release potassium chloride tablets and dissolve in warm water for tube administration

rationales.correct: Aspiration prevention and tube patency require semi-Fowler's elevation of 30-45 degrees (A), radiographic verification before initial use (B), scheduled water flushes (C), and monitoring external tube length/pH checks (D).

incorrect.rationale: Auscultation of air insufflation is unreliable and contraindicated as a verification method because bronchial placement can mimic gastric sounds.
Extended-release tablets must never be crushed due to risk of rapid dose dumping and toxicity.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Implements evidence-based aspiration and medication safety standards for enteral nutrition.

patient_profile.history: C4 complete spinal cord injury sustained in a motor vehicle collision 2 hours ago

assessment.neurological: Quadriplegia, loss of sensation below clavicles
assessment.integumentary: Warm, dry, flushed skin below level of injury

questions.stem: The nurse identifies neurogenic shock. Which clinical manifestations and pathophysiological mechanisms are consistent with this condition? Select all that apply.

options.text: Loss of sympathetic vasomotor tone below the C4 lesion causing massive venous and arterial vasodilation
Unopposed parasympathetic vagal stimulation resulting in severe bradycardia
Warm, dry skin due to peripheral vasodilation and inability to vasoconstrict
Poikilothermia (impaired thermoregulation) requiring active external warming measures
High risk for venous thromboembolism due to venous pooling and immobility
Compensatory sinus tachycardia with cool, clammy, diaphoretic extremities
Severe hypertension triggered by noxious bladder distension

rationales.correct: High cervical spinal cord injury (above T6) disrupts descending sympathetic pathways while leaving cranial nerve X (vagus) parasympathetic outflow intact. This produces distributive neurogenic shock: profound vasodilation/hypotension (A), bradycardia (B), warm dry skin (C), loss of thermoregulation (D), and venous stasis/DVT risk (E).

incorrect.rationale: Tachycardia with cool, clammy skin characterizes hypovolemic or cardiogenic shock, not neurogenic shock.
Severe hypertension from noxious stimuli is autonomic dysreflexia, which occurs after spinal shock resolves, not in acute neurogenic shock.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Distinguishes neurogenic shock from hypovolemic shock and autonomic dysreflexia following cervical SCI.

patient_profile.history: Newly diagnosed Burkitt lymphoma; initiated aggressive multi-agent chemotherapy 18 hours ago

assessment.cardiovascular: Peaked T waves on cardiac monitor

questions.stem: The patient has developed Tumor Lysis Syndrome (TLS). Which anticipated orders and nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Initiate aggressive intravenous hydration with 0.9% sodium chloride at 200 mL/hr
Administer rasburicase IV as prescribed to rapidly convert uric acid to soluble allantoin
Administer IV calcium gluconate to stabilize the myocardium against hyperkalemia
Administer IV regular insulin with 50% dextrose to shift potassium intracellularly
Eliminate all potassium and phosphorus from IV fluids and dietary intake
Administer IV potassium chloride 20 mEq/hr to protect renal tubular function
Administer calcium acetate or sevelamer to bind dietary phosphate

rationales.correct: Rapid lysis of high-grade lymphoma cells releases intracellular potassium, phosphate, and nucleic acids (uric acid), causing hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, secondary hypocalcemia, and uric acid nephropathy. Management includes aggressive IV hydration (A), rasburicase for severe hyperuricemia (B), cardiac membrane stabilization with calcium gluconate (C), insulin/dextrose for potassium shifting (D), strict potassium/phosphate restriction (E), and phosphate binders (G).

incorrect.rationale: Potassium administration is lethal in severe hyperkalemia (6.4 mEq/L).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Formulates comprehensive emergency management for Tumor Lysis Syndrome electrolyte and renal derangements.

patient_profile.history: G4P4, 45 minutes after vaginal delivery of a 4,450-g newborn following prolonged oxytocin-augmented labor

assessment.obstetric: Boggy uterine fundus palpated 3 cm above the umbilicus and deviated to the right; saturating two peripads in 15 minutes with bright red blood and large clots

questions.stem: Which nursing interventions are appropriate for managing this patient's postpartum hemorrhage? Select all that apply.

options.text: Perform firm bimanual uterine fundal massage while supporting the lower uterine segment
Insert a straight urinary catheter to empty the distended bladder
Initiate a rapid IV oxytocin infusion via a second large-bore IV line
Verify the patient has no history of hypertension prior to administering methylergonovine
Verify the patient has no history of asthma prior to administering carboprost tromethamine
Quantify cumulative blood loss by weighing blood-soaked pads and underpads
Administer methylergonovine via rapid IV push for faster uterine contraction
Place the patient in high-Fowler's position to promote lochial drainage

rationales.correct: Uterine atony is the leading cause of postpartum hemorrhage, exacerbated here by multiparity, macrosomia, and a full bladder (fundus displaced to the right). Priority actions include fundal massage with lower-segment support (A), bladder emptying (B), IV oxytocin (C), checking contraindications for second-line uterotonics—hypertension for methylergonovine (D) and asthma for carboprost (E)—and quantitative blood loss measurement (F).

incorrect.rationale: IV push methylergonovine causes hypertensive crisis and stroke; it must be given IM.
High-Fowler's position worsens cerebral hypoperfusion during hemorrhagic shock.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Executes multi-modal uterine atony rescue while enforcing uterotonic safety checks.

patient_profile.history: Small cell lung cancer admitted with lethargy and confusion

assessment.neurological: Drowsy, oriented to person and place only
assessment.cardiovascular: No peripheral edema, flat neck veins

questions.stem: The nurse identifies Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuretic Hormone Secretion (SIADH). Which interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Implement strict free water fluid restriction (800 to 1,000 mL/day) as prescribed
Initiate seizure precautions including padded side rails and suction at bedside
Administer 3% hypertonic saline via an infusion pump at a controlled slow rate if ordered for neurologic symptoms
Monitor serum sodium every 2 to 4 hours so correction does not exceed 8 to 10 mEq/L in 24 hours
Monitor strict intake and output and daily weights
Infuse 0.45% sodium chloride at 125 mL/hr to replace urinary sodium losses
Administer desmopressin (DDAVP) 2 mcg IV to conserve free water

rationales.correct: Small cell lung cancer causes ectopic ADH secretion (SIADH), producing euvolemic hypotonic hyponatremia with concentrated urine. Treatment includes fluid restriction (A), seizure precautions for Na <120 mEq/L (B), cautious 3% hypertonic saline for symptomatic neurological deficits (C), frequent sodium monitoring to prevent osmotic demyelination syndrome (D), and strict I&O/daily weights (E).

incorrect.rationale: Hypotonic saline worsens cerebral edema and hyponatremia in SIADH.
Desmopressin is an ADH analog used for diabetes insipidus and would exacerbate SIADH.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Plans safe correction of severe SIADH hyponatremia while preventing osmotic demyelination.

patient_profile.history: Treatment-resistant bipolar I disorder stabilized on lithium carbonate 600 mg PO twice daily

assessment.neurological: Coarse hand tremor, slurred speech, ataxia
assessment.gastrointestinal: Persistent diarrhea for 2 days

questions.stem: Which statements and nursing actions accurately apply to lithium toxicity management and prevention? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hold all scheduled doses of lithium carbonate immediately and notify the provider
Initiate IV 0.9% sodium chloride infusion to restore sodium and promote renal lithium clearance
Instruct the patient to avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen and naproxen because they increase lithium levels
Teach the patient that dehydration and sodium depletion precipitate lithium retention in the kidneys
Prepare for possible hemodialysis if neurological deterioration progresses or levels exceed 2.5 mEq/L
Advise the patient to follow a strict low-sodium diet to prevent fluid retention
Administer hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg PO to promote renal excretion of lithium

rationales.correct: Lithium is handled by the proximal renal tubule identically to sodium; hyponatremia and dehydration from diarrhea cause increased renal lithium reabsorption and toxicity (serum lithium 2.1 mEq/L, coarse tremor, ataxia, slurred speech). Interventions include holding lithium (A), IV 0.9% saline resuscitation (B), educating against NSAIDs (C) and sodium/fluid depletion (D), and anticipating dialysis if severe (E).

incorrect.rationale: Low-sodium diets increase renal lithium reabsorption and cause toxicity; consistent normal sodium intake is essential.
Thiazide diuretics cause sodium depletion and markedly increase serum lithium levels.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies diarrhea-induced hyponatremic lithium toxicity and initiates sodium/volume restoration.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative laryngectomy with a cuffed tracheostomy tube placed 48 hours ago

assessment.respiratory: Coarse rhonchi over trachea, audible gurgling, patient coughing weakly

questions.stem: Which principles must the nurse follow when performing endotracheal suctioning via the tracheostomy tube? Select all that apply.

options.text: Hyperoxygenate the patient with 100% oxygen for 30 to 60 seconds prior to suctioning
Maintain strict surgical asepsis (sterile technique) throughout the procedure
Apply intermittent suction only while withdrawing the catheter, limiting each pass to 10 to 15 seconds
Select a suction catheter whose outer diameter does not exceed half the internal diameter of the tracheostomy tube
Allow at least 1 minute between suction passes for oxygenation and heart rate recovery
Instill 5 mL of sterile normal saline into the tracheostomy tube prior to each pass to thin secretions
Apply continuous suction while inserting the catheter until resistance is met

rationales.correct: Safe tracheostomy suctioning requires pre-oxygenation (A), sterile technique (B), intermittent suction on withdrawal for <=10-15 seconds (C), appropriate catheter sizing (<50% internal lumen) to prevent atelectasis (D), and recovery intervals between passes (E).

incorrect.rationale: Routine normal saline instillation dislodges bacterial biofilm into the lower airways, impairs oxygenation, and is no longer recommended.
Applying suction during insertion causes tracheal mucosal trauma and hypoxemia.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Executes evidence-based sterile tracheostomy suctioning while avoiding mucosal injury and hypoxemia.

patient_profile.history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus admitted with severe dehydration and altered mental status

questions.stem: For each clinical finding below, specify whether it is characteristic of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS), or Both.

rows.label: Blood glucose typically >600 mg/dL with serum osmolality >320 mOsm/kg
Arterial pH <7.30 with positive serum ketones and Kussmaul respirations
Profound osmotic diuresis requiring aggressive IV isotonic fluid resuscitation first
Endogenous insulin levels sufficient to prevent lipolysis and ketogenesis

rationales.correct: HHS features extreme hyperglycemia (>600 mg/dL) and hyperosmolality (>320 mOsm/kg) without significant ketoacidosis because residual endogenous insulin suppresses lipolysis. DKA features ketoacidosis (pH <7.30, ketones, Kussmaul respirations). Both require aggressive initial isotonic fluid resuscitation to restore intravascular volume.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Differentiates pathophysiology and diagnostic criteria of DKA vs. HHS.

patient_profile.history: G3P2 at 33 weeks gestation presenting to obstetric triage with vaginal bleeding

assessment.obstetric: Uterus is rigid, board-like, and exquisitely tender to palpation; continuous uterine contractions

questions.stem: Classify each clinical feature as characteristic of Placental Abruption or Placenta Previa.

rows.label: Sudden onset of painless, bright red vaginal bleeding with a soft, non-tender uterus
Dark red vaginal bleeding accompanied by severe abdominal pain and a rigid, board-like uterus
Strong association with chronic hypertension, preeclampsia, and cocaine use
High risk for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) due to retroplacental clot consumption

rationales.correct: Placenta previa presents with painless bright red bleeding and a soft uterus. Placental abruption involves premature separation of a normally implanted placenta, strongly linked to hypertension/vasoconstriction, presenting with painful dark bleeding, uterine hypertonicity/rigidity, and high risk of DIC.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Distinguishes third-trimester hemorrhage etiologies (abruption vs. previa).

patient_profile.history: Severe COPD admitted with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure

assessment.respiratory: Shallow respirations, barrel chest, pursed-lip breathing

questions.stem: Evaluate each arterial blood gas set and identify its correct acid-base interpretation.

rows.label: pH 7.32, PaCO2 64 mmHg, HCO3- 32 mEq/L
pH 7.24, PaCO2 26 mmHg, HCO3- 11 mEq/L
pH 7.50, PaCO2 42 mmHg, HCO3- 33 mEq/L

rationales.correct: R1 shows acidemia (7.32) driven by elevated PaCO2 (64) with renal HCO3- retention (32) partially compensating -> Partially Compensated Respiratory Acidosis. R2 shows acidemia (7.24) driven by low HCO3- (11) with hyperventilation lowering PaCO2 (26) -> Partially Compensated Metabolic Acidosis. R3 shows alkalemia (7.50) driven by elevated HCO3- (33) with normal PaCO2 (42) -> Uncompensated Metabolic Alkalosis.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Accurately interprets primary acid-base disorders and degree of compensation.

patient_profile.history: Brought to ED at 0200 with sudden barking cough and hoarseness

assessment.respiratory: Inspiratory stridor at rest, suprasternal retractions, barking seal-like cough

questions.stem: Indicate whether each nursing intervention is Indicated or Contraindicated for a toddler with acute laryngotracheobronchitis (croup) and stridor at rest.

rows.label: Administer nebulized racemic epinephrine and single-dose oral/IM dexamethasone
Monitor the child continuously for 2 to 4 hours after racemic epinephrine for rebound airway edema
Administer an oral sedative such as diphenhydramine to help the child sleep
Keep the child calm in the parent's arms and provide cool humidified oxygen

rationales.correct: Stridor at rest in croup requires nebulized racemic epinephrine (vasoconstriction of subglottic mucosa) plus corticosteroids (dexamethasone) to prevent rebound edema, alongside mandatory 2-4 hour post-nebulizer observation and calm comfort measures. Sedatives are contraindicated because they mask worsening hypoxia and depress respiratory drive.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Differentiates safe vs. hazardous interventions in moderate-to-severe pediatric croup.

patient_profile.history: Severe traumatic brain injury with external ventricular drain (EVD) monitoring intracranial pressure

questions.stem: Specify whether each nursing intervention will Decrease ICP or Increase ICP in this patient.

rows.label: Maintain head of bed at 30 degrees with head and neck in neutral midline alignment
Cluster suctioning, turning, and bathing together to minimize interruptions
Administer prescribed stool softeners and maintain normothermia
Allow sustained hypercapnia (PaCO2 >50 mmHg) to promote cerebral vasodilation

rationales.correct: HOB at 30 degrees with neutral alignment enhances jugular venous outflow (decreases ICP). Preventing Valsalva straining and fever prevents metabolic/pressure spikes (decreases ICP). Clustering nursing care causes cumulative ICP surges, and hypercapnia causes potent cerebral vasodilation that raises intracranial blood volume and ICP.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Evaluates physiological effects of nursing care on intracranial dynamics.

patient_profile.history: Admitted from skilled nursing facility with profuse watery diarrhea following clindamycin therapy

assessment.gastrointestinal: Hyperactive bowel sounds, mild lower abdominal cramping

questions.stem: Determine whether each infection prevention action is Correct or Incorrect for a patient with Clostridioides difficile infection.

rows.label: Perform hand hygiene using soap and water friction for at least 20 seconds upon exiting the room
Use alcohol-based hand sanitizer after removing gloves when hands are not visibly soiled
Disinfect shared equipment and room surfaces using an EPA-registered sporicidal bleach solution
Don clean gown and gloves prior to entering the patient's room

rationales.correct: C. difficile forms hardy bacterial spores that are resistant to alcohol-based hand rubs and standard quaternary ammonium disinfectants. Mechanical handwashing with soap and water (R1), sporicidal hypochlorite/bleach disinfection (R3), and Contact Precautions with gown and gloves (R4) are mandatory.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Applies spore-specific contact isolation and hand hygiene rules for C. difficile.

patient_profile.history: 3 hours post-coronary artery bypass grafting with mediastinal chest tubes

assessment.cardiovascular: Muffled heart sounds, jugular venous distension, chest tube drainage suddenly dropped from 150 mL/hr to 0 mL/hr over the last hour

questions.stem: Complete the clinical judgment statement regarding the patient's acute postoperative deterioration.

segments.text_before: The patient is most likely experiencing

options.text: acute cardiac tamponade
a tension pneumothorax
hypovolemic shock from active bleeding

segments.text_before: and the nurse's priority action is to

options.text: aggressively strip and milk the mediastinal chest tube
notify the cardiothoracic surgeon immediately for emergent pericardiocentesis or re-exploration
administer IV furosemide 40 mg to reduce jugular venous distension

rationales.correct: Beck's triad (hypotension with narrowed pulse pressure, JVD, muffled heart sounds) plus pulsus paradoxus and abrupt cessation of mediastinal chest tube output post-CABG indicates acute cardiac tamponade from clot occlusion. Immediate surgical intervention is required; aggressively stripping chest tubes creates dangerous negative pressures that damage mediastinal tissues.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies Beck's triad and obstructed chest tube drainage as acute cardiac tamponade requiring emergent surgical decompression.

patient_profile.history: G1P0 at 40 weeks gestation receiving IV oxytocin augmentation at 14 mU/min

assessment.obstetric: Uterine contractions occurring every 90 seconds lasting 85 seconds; fetal heart rate shows recurrent decelerations beginning after the peak of each contraction and returning to baseline after the contraction ends

questions.stem: Complete the fetal monitoring interpretation and nursing action statement.

segments.text_before: The fetal heart rate tracing demonstrates

options.text: early decelerations
variable decelerations
late decelerations

segments.text_after: while repositioning the patient onto her left side.

options.text: discontinue the IV oxytocin infusion
prepare for immediate amnioinfusion
assist the patient to push with contractions

rationales.correct: Decelerations starting after the contraction peak and recovering after the contraction ends are late decelerations (VEAL CHOP: Late = Placental insufficiency), precipitated here by oxytocin-induced uterine tachysystole (>5 contractions in 10 minutes). Stopping oxytocin immediately reduces uterine tone and restores placental perfusion.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Applies VEAL CHOP interpretation to identify late decelerations from tachysystole and halts oxytocin.

patient_profile.history: Brought to ED 3 hours after ingesting 40 tablets of acetaminophen 500 mg

assessment.gastrointestinal: Mild nausea and diaphoresis

questions.stem: Complete the toxicological management statement.

segments.text_before: To prevent fulminant hepatic necrosis, the nurse must administer

options.text: flumazenil
N-acetylcysteine
physostigmine

segments.text_after: stores to detoxify the toxic metabolite NAPQI.

options.text: glutathione
vitamin K
acetylcholine

rationales.correct: Acetaminophen overdose depletes hepatic glutathione, allowing accumulation of the hepatotoxic metabolite NAPQI. N-acetylcysteine (NAC) restores glutathione stores and prevents centrilobular hepatic necrosis.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies N-acetylcysteine and its glutathione-replenishing mechanism in acetaminophen toxicity.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative total knee arthroplasty 3 days ago; sudden onset pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea

assessment.respiratory: Tachypneic, clear lung sounds bilaterally
assessment.cardiovascular: Tachycardic, right calf swollen and tender

diagnostic_results.findings: Large filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery

questions.stem: Complete the clinical action statement for this patient.

segments.text_before: After applying high-flow supplemental oxygen and elevating the head of the bed, the nurse should anticipate initiating

options.text: continuous IV unfractionated heparin
oral warfarin monotherapy
IV protamine sulfate
extension of existing thrombus and recurrent embolization
immediate enzymatic dissolution of the embolus
rebound hypercoagulability from protein C depletion

rationales.correct: In acute hemodynamically stable pulmonary embolism, immediate parenteral anticoagulation (unfractionated heparin or LMWH) prevents clot propagation and recurrent fatal emboli while endogenous fibrinolysis clears the clot. Heparin does not directly dissolve existing clots (unlike alteplase).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Selects immediate parenteral anticoagulation and understands its mechanism in acute PE.

patient_profile.history: Brought to ED with fever, photophobia, severe headache, and petechial rash on trunk

assessment.neurological: Nuchal rigidity; flexing the child's neck produces involuntary flexion of the hips and knees

questions.stem: Complete the pediatric meningitis assessment and isolation statement.

segments.text_before: The involuntary flexion of the hips and knees when the neck is flexed is a positive

options.text: Brudzinski
Kernig
Chvostek

segments.text_before: and because of the petechial rash suggesting Neisseria meningitidis, the nurse must immediately place the child on

options.text: droplet
airborne
protective

rationales.correct: Neck flexion causing involuntary hip/knee flexion is a positive Brudzinski sign (Kernig sign is pain/resistance on knee extension with hip flexed). Suspected bacterial/meningococcal meningitis requires immediate Droplet Precautions (surgical mask within 3 feet) for the first 24 hours of effective antibiotic therapy.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies Brudzinski sign and institutes immediate Droplet Precautions for meningococcal meningitis.

patient_profile.history: Heavy alcohol use; admitted with severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and persistent vomiting

assessment.gastrointestinal: Guarding in epigastrium, hypoactive bowel sounds, bluish discoloration around the umbilicus

questions.stem: Complete the clinical interpretation for this patient with acute pancreatitis.

segments.text_before: The periumbilical ecchymosis is documented as a positive

options.text: Cullen
Grey Turner
Murphy
retroperitoneal hemorrhage from severe necrotizing pancreatitis
acute ascending cholangitis
portal vein thrombosis

rationales.correct: Cullen sign (periumbilical ecchymosis) and Grey Turner sign (flank ecchymosis) signify retroperitoneal hemorrhage tracking along fascial planes in severe hemorrhagic/necrotizing pancreatitis, carrying high mortality and hypovolemic shock risk.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes Cullen sign as an indicator of hemorrhagic/necrotizing pancreatitis.

patient_profile.history: Right hemispheric ischemic stroke 24 hours ago

questions.stem: Review the nurse's shift assessment note below. Highlight the findings that require immediate intervention or indicate high aspiration/safety risk.

interaction.passage: Patient is alert and oriented to person and place. Left-sided hemiplegia noted with 0/5 strength in left upper and lower extremities. Patient demonstrates left unilateral spatial neglect, ignoring food on the left side of the tray. During bedside water swallow screen, the patient coughs immediately after sipping and exhibits a wet, gurgly voice quality. Bowel sounds are normoactive in all four quadrants, and an indwelling urinary catheter is draining clear yellow urine at 45 mL/hr.

segments.text: alert and oriented to person and place
demonstrates left unilateral spatial neglect, ignoring food on the left side of the tray
coughs immediately after sipping and exhibits a wet, gurgly voice quality
Bowel sounds are normoactive in all four quadrants
draining clear yellow urine at 45 mL/hr

rationales.correct: Coughing after swallowing and a wet/gurgly voice (T3) indicate silent/overt pharyngeal dysphagia and high aspiration pneumonia risk, requiring strict NPO status until formal speech-language pathology evaluation. Left unilateral neglect (T2) poses a major safety/fall and nutritional risk requiring environmental scanning cues.

incorrect.rationale: Alertness is a reassuring baseline finding.
Normoactive bowel sounds are normal.
Clear urine at 45 mL/hr indicates adequate renal perfusion.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies post-stroke dysphagia and unilateral neglect cues requiring immediate safety precautions.

patient_profile.history: Term newborn delivered at 39 weeks to a mother with gestational diabetes mellitus

questions.stem: Highlight the findings in the newborn nursery note that indicate neonatal hypoglycemia requiring immediate point-of-care glucose testing and feeding.

interaction.passage: Term male infant of diabetic mother at 6 hours of life. Skin is pink with mild acrocyanosis of hands and feet. Infant exhibits coarse jitteriness of both hands and a high-pitched, weak cry. Axillary temperature is 36.1°C, and the infant demonstrates poor suck reflex during attempted breastfeeding. Passively flexed extremities with brisk recoil noted.

segments.text: mild acrocyanosis of hands and feet
coarse jitteriness of both hands and a high-pitched, weak cry
Axillary temperature is 36.1°C
poor suck reflex during attempted breastfeeding
Passively flexed extremities with brisk recoil

rationales.correct: Infants of diabetic mothers experience rebound hyperinsulinemia after cord clamping. Coarse jitteriness/tremors and high-pitched cry (T2), hypothermia <36.5°C (T3), and lethargy/poor feeding (T4) are hallmark signs of neonatal hypoglycemia.

incorrect.rationale: Acrocyanosis is a normal benign vasomotor finding in the first 24-48 hours of life.
Flexed extremities with brisk recoil indicate normal term neuromuscular tone.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies neuroglycopenic and autonomic cues of neonatal hypoglycemia in an infant of a diabetic mother.

patient_profile.history: Receiving IV ceftriaxone for community-acquired pneumonia

questions.stem: Highlight the findings in the triage note that indicate an acute IgE-mediated anaphylactic reaction requiring immediate intramuscular epinephrine.

interaction.passage: Five minutes after starting IV ceftriaxone, the patient reports diffuse pruritus and generalized urticaria across her chest and arms. Audible inspiratory stridor and diffuse expiratory wheezing are present along with visible lip and tongue angioedema. Blood pressure dropped from 124/78 mmHg to 84/48 mmHg. Patient has a small non-blanching bruise on her left forearm from venipuncture.

segments.text: diffuse pruritus and generalized urticaria across her chest and arms
Audible inspiratory stridor and diffuse expiratory wheezing
visible lip and tongue angioedema
Blood pressure dropped from 124/78 mmHg to 84/48 mmHg
small non-blanching bruise on her left forearm from venipuncture

rationales.correct: Anaphylaxis is a rapid multi-system hypersensitivity reaction involving mucocutaneous symptoms (urticaria/angioedema: T1, T3), upper/lower airway compromise (stridor/wheezing: T2), and distributive hypotension (T4), requiring immediate IM epinephrine 0.3-0.5 mg in the anterolateral thigh.

incorrect.rationale: A localized venipuncture ecchymosis is unrelated to anaphylaxis.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes multi-system criteria of anaphylactic shock.

patient_profile.history: Graves' disease admitted for non-cardiac emergency surgery

questions.stem: Highlight the findings in the postoperative progress note that indicate the onset of life-threatening thyroid storm.

interaction.passage: Two hours postoperatively, the patient became severely agitated, delirious, and diaphoretic. Core temperature rose rapidly to 40.1°C. Cardiac monitor shows atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 156 bpm and blood pressure of 168/94 mmHg. Patient also reports mild incisional tenderness and has hypoactive bowel sounds following general anesthesia.

segments.text: severely agitated, delirious, and diaphoretic
Core temperature rose rapidly to 40.1°C
atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response of 156 bpm
mild incisional tenderness
hypoactive bowel sounds following general anesthesia

rationales.correct: Thyroid storm (thyrotoxic crisis) is precipitated by surgical stress in hyperthyroid patients and manifests with severe CNS delirium/agitation (T1), extreme hyperpyrexia (T2), and severe tachyarrhythmias/atrial fibrillation (T3).

incorrect.rationale: Mild incisional tenderness is expected postoperatively.
Hypoactive bowel sounds are expected shortly after general anesthesia.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies the diagnostic triad of thyroid storm (CNS dysfunction, hyperthermia, severe tachycardia).

patient_profile.history: Sickle cell disease (HbSS) admitted with vaso-occlusive pain crisis

questions.stem: Highlight the findings in the clinical note that indicate progression to Acute Chest Syndrome (ACS).

interaction.passage: Patient initially admitted for bilateral femur bone pain. On hospital day 2, patient developed new-onset pleuritic chest pain, tachypnea at 28 breaths/min, and a fever of 38.6°C. Pulse oximetry dropped from 97% to 88% on room air, and auscultation reveals new crackles in the right lower lung field. Patient's bilateral femur pain has improved from 9/10 to 4/10 after IV hydromorphone.

segments.text: new-onset pleuritic chest pain
tachypnea at 28 breaths/min, and a fever of 38.6°C
Pulse oximetry dropped from 97% to 88% on room air
new crackles in the right lower lung field
bilateral femur pain has improved from 9/10 to 4/10

rationales.correct: Acute chest syndrome is the leading cause of death in sickle cell disease and is diagnosed by a new pulmonary infiltrate (crackles: T4) accompanied by fever (T2), chest pain (T1), tachypnea (T2), and hypoxemia (T3).

incorrect.rationale: Improvement in extremity bone pain reflects analgesic response and is not a diagnostic feature of ACS.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies acute chest syndrome in a sickle cell patient requiring incentive spirometry, antibiotics, oxygen, and exchange transfusion.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative day 6 open abdominal colectomy; obese with type 2 diabetes

questions.stem: Highlight the findings in the surgical wound assessment that indicate impending wound dehiscence and evisceration.

interaction.passage: Following an episode of forceful coughing, the patient reports a sudden 'popping' sensation at her midline abdominal incision. Upon inspection, the surgical dressing is saturated with a large amount of serosanguinous fluid, and a 4-cm separation of the fascial wound edges is visible with a loop of bowel protruding slightly. Surrounding skin shows well-approximated staples at the superior margin without purulent drainage.

segments.text: sudden 'popping' sensation at her midline abdominal incision
saturated with a large amount of serosanguinous fluid
4-cm separation of the fascial wound edges is visible with a loop of bowel protruding
well-approximated staples at the superior margin without purulent drainage

rationales.correct: A sudden popping sensation after coughing (T1) followed by a gush of pink serosanguinous fluid (T2) and fascial separation with bowel protrusion (T3) defines surgical wound dehiscence and evisceration. Immediate nursing action is covering the viscera with sterile saline-moistened gauze, placing the patient in low-Fowler's with knees bent, and calling the surgeon.

incorrect.rationale: Intact staples and lack of purulence are normal/benign findings.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies classic warning signs and presentation of abdominal wound dehiscence/evisceration.

patient_profile.history: Chronic kidney disease stage 4 admitted for pneumonia

assessment.cardiovascular: Trace ankle edema

questions.stem: Review the patient's morning laboratory table. Highlight the critical results that require immediate provider notification and cardiac monitoring.

rationales.correct: Serum potassium of 6.6 mEq/L (C1) is a critical panic value capable of causing fatal ventricular fibrillation or asystole, requiring immediate ECG monitoring, IV calcium gluconate, and potassium-shifting therapy. Creatinine 3.4 mg/dL, Hgb 10.2 g/dL, and phosphorus 5.4 mg/dL are expected chronic findings in stage 4 CKD.

incorrect.rationale: Expected baseline elevation in stage 4 CKD.
Expected normocytic anemia of CKD from reduced erythropoietin.
Normal serum sodium.
Mildly elevated phosphorus is typical in stage 4 CKD and not an immediate cardiac emergency.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Differentiates an acute life-threatening critical electrolyte value from expected baseline CKD laboratory abnormalities.

patient_profile.history: Receiving IV vancomycin, gentamicin, enoxaparin, and phenytoin

questions.stem: Highlight the drug levels in the therapeutic monitoring table that are supratherapeutic (toxic) and require holding the next scheduled dose.

rationales.correct: Both vancomycin trough (28 mcg/mL > 20 mcg/mL) and gentamicin trough (3.4 mcg/mL > 2.0 mcg/mL) are supratherapeutic and indicate impaired renal clearance with high risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity. Both doses must be held and the provider/pharmacist notified.

incorrect.rationale: Phenytoin 14 mcg/mL is within the therapeutic window (10-20 mcg/mL).
Valproic acid 75 mcg/mL is within the therapeutic window (50-100 mcg/mL).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies toxic aminoglycoside and glycopeptide trough levels to prevent nephrotoxicity/ototoxicity.

patient_profile.history: Septic shock following retained placental tissue; oozing blood from all venipuncture sites

assessment.integumentary: Petechiae, purpura, bleeding from gums and IV catheters

questions.stem: Highlight all laboratory values in the coagulation panel that confirm Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC).

rationales.correct: DIC is characterized by widespread microvascular fibrin deposition that consumes platelets (38,000/mm³) and clotting factors/fibrinogen (78 mg/dL), prolonging PT/INR (28.4 sec / 2.7), while secondary fibrinolysis markedly elevates fibrin degradation products/D-dimer (6,800 ng/mL).

incorrect.rationale: Serum albumin 3.6 g/dL is normal and not a diagnostic marker of DIC.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies the classic consumptive coagulopathy lab profile of DIC.

patient_profile.history: G1P0 at 35 weeks gestation presenting with right upper quadrant epigastric pain, nausea, and malaise

assessment.gastrointestinal: Right upper quadrant tenderness

questions.stem: Highlight the laboratory findings in the obstetric panel that confirm HELLP syndrome.

rationales.correct: HELLP syndrome stands for Hemolysis (elevated LDH 890 U/L and schistocytes on peripheral smear: C3, C4), Elevated Liver enzymes (AST/ALT 340/295 U/L: C1), and Low Platelets (<100,000/mm³: C2). Definitive treatment is maternal stabilization and delivery.

incorrect.rationale: Fasting blood glucose of 88 mg/dL is normal.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies the diagnostic triad of HELLP syndrome from obstetric laboratory values.

patient_profile.history: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 30%) presenting with worsening orthopnea

assessment.respiratory: Bibasilar crackles
assessment.cardiovascular: S3 gallop, 3+ pitting edema

questions.stem: Highlight the laboratory findings that support acute decompensated heart failure and cardiorenal congestion.

rationales.correct: BNP >1,800 pg/mL reflects severe ventricular wall stretch/volume overload (C1). Hypervolemic dilutional hyponatremia (129 mEq/L: C2) and mild transaminase elevation from passive hepatic venous congestion (C4) are classic in acute decompensated heart failure.

incorrect.rationale: Serum calcium of 9.2 mg/dL is normal.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Interprets BNP, dilutional hyponatremia, and congestive hepatopathy in acute heart failure.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with community-acquired pneumonia and sepsis; blood cultures pending

questions.stem: Review the Medication Administration Record (MAR) below. Highlight the medication orders that require clarification with the provider before administration.

cells: Every 24 hours (Allergy: Penicillin - mild rash 10 yrs ago)

rationales.correct: Vancomycin must be infused slowly over at least 60 minutes (never IV push) to prevent severe histamine-mediated infusion reactions ('Red Man syndrome') and hypotension (C2). Concentrated potassium chloride must NEVER be administered undiluted or IV push because it causes immediate fatal cardiac arrest (C4).

incorrect.rationale: Third-generation cephalosporins like ceftriaxone have negligible cross-reactivity with non-anaphylactic penicillin rash.
Enoxaparin 40 mg SubQ daily is appropriate DVT prophylaxis with normal platelets.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Intercepts lethal IV push potassium and rapid vancomycin orders on the MAR.

patient_profile.history: T4 complete spinal cord injury 8 months ago, admitted for urinary tract infection

assessment.neurological: Sudden pounding headache, blurred vision, nasal congestion
assessment.integumentary: Profuse diaphoresis and flushing above the nipple line; pale, cool skin with piloerection below T4
assessment.genitourinary: Indwelling urinary catheter tubing kinked under patient's thigh; bladder distended

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie clinical judgment model by selecting the most likely condition, two priority nursing actions, and two parameters to monitor.

action_options.text: Place the patient immediately in an upright high-Fowler's (90-degree) position
