Unkink the urinary catheter tubing and check for bladder distension or fecal impaction
Place the patient in flat supine position with legs elevated
Administer IV atropine 1 mg push for reflex bradycardia

parameter_options.text: Blood pressure every 2 to 5 minutes
Urine output and bladder decompression
Patellar deep tendon reflexes

rationales.correct: Patients with SCI at or above T6 are at risk for autonomic dysreflexia triggered by noxious stimuli below the lesion (kinked catheter/distended bladder). Unopposed sympathetic discharge below T6 causes severe vasoconstriction and life-threatening hypertension (214/118 mmHg), while baroreceptor vagal reflex causes bradycardia (46 bpm) and flushing/sweating above T6. Immediate upright positioning (A1) lowers BP orthostatically, and relieving the noxious urinary obstruction (A2) resolves the crisis while monitoring BP (P1) and urine flow (P2).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies autonomic dysreflexia in a T4 SCI patient and executes orthostatic and stimulus-removal interventions.

patient_profile.history: G1P0 at 36 weeks gestation with gestational hypertension

assessment.neurological: Severe unremitting frontal headache, visual scotomata (spots), hyperreflexia (4+ patellar reflexes) with 3 beats of ankle clonus
assessment.gastrointestinal: Epigastric right upper quadrant pain

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie diagram for this antepartum patient.

action_options.text: Initiate IV magnesium sulfate loading dose and maintenance infusion for seizure prophylaxis
Administer IV labetalol or hydralazine as ordered to lower severe-range blood pressure
Encourage ambulation in the hallway to reduce peripheral edema
Restrict dietary sodium to <500 mg/day and administer furosemide

parameter_options.text: Deep tendon reflexes, respiratory rate, and hourly urine output
Continuous fetal heart rate and maternal blood pressure
Fasting serum cholesterol levels

rationales.correct: Severe-range BP (>=160/110 mmHg), proteinuria, cerebral/visual symptoms, epigastric pain, and clonus indicate preeclampsia with severe features (impending eclampsia). Magnesium sulfate prevents eclamptic seizures (A1), IV antihypertensives prevent maternal hemorrhagic stroke (A2), and monitoring DTRs/RR/urine output (P1) plus BP/FHR (P2) ensures maternal-fetal safety.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Formulates seizure prophylaxis and stroke prevention for preeclampsia with severe features.

patient_profile.history: Long-standing hypothyroidism; stopped taking levothyroxine 2 months ago; admitted with pneumonia

assessment.neurological: Stuporous, hypothermic, non-pitting periorbital and generalized edema

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie diagram for this endocrine emergency.

action_options.text: Maintain airway patency and prepare for mechanical ventilation
Administer IV levothyroxine and IV hydrocortisone as prescribed, using passive rewarming blankets
Apply active rapid external warming blankets to raise core temperature by 3°C/hr
Administer IV propranolol and propylthiouracil

parameter_options.text: Cardiac rhythm and blood pressure during thyroid hormone replacement
Arterial blood gases and respiratory status
Serum uric acid levels

rationales.correct: Myxedema coma is decompensated hypothyroidism triggered by infection/medication cessation, presenting with hypothermia, hypoventilation, bradycardia, hypotension, hyponatremia, and stupor. Airway/ventilatory support (A1) and IV levothyroxine plus hydrocortisone (to cover concurrent adrenal insufficiency) with gradual passive rewarming (A2—active rewarming causes peripheral vasodilation and vascular collapse) are essential.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies myxedema coma and selects safe airway, hormone replacement, and passive warming strategies.

patient_profile.history: Blunt chest trauma from steering wheel impact in motor vehicle crash

assessment.respiratory: Severe dyspnea, absent breath sounds over left hemithorax, hyperresonance to percussion on the left, trachea deviated to the right
assessment.cardiovascular: Marked jugular venous distension

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie diagram for this trauma emergency.

action_options.text: Prepare immediately for emergent needle thoracostomy decompression followed by chest tube insertion
Administer 100% high-flow supplemental oxygen and establish two large-bore IV lines
Send the patient to radiology for a portable chest radiograph before intervening
Initiate positive-pressure bag-valve-mask ventilation prior to chest decompression

parameter_options.text: Tracheal alignment and bilateral breath sounds
Blood pressure, heart rate, and oxygen saturation
Serum amylase and lipase

rationales.correct: Absent unilateral breath sounds with hyperresonance (vs. dullness in hemothorax), contralateral tracheal deviation, JVD, and obstructive shock define tension pneumothorax. It is a clinical diagnosis requiring immediate needle decompression without waiting for chest X-ray (A1, A2).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies tension pneumothorax clinically and initiates immediate decompression.

patient_profile.history: Full-term firstborn male presenting with progressive non-bilious vomiting after every feeding

assessment.gastrointestinal: Forceful projectile vomiting, visible left-to-right gastric peristaltic waves, firm olive-shaped mass palpated in right upper quadrant; infant eagerly wants to feed again immediately after vomiting

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie diagram for this infant.

action_options.text: Keep the infant NPO and insert a nasogastric tube to low intermittent suction if ordered
Initiate IV fluid resuscitation and electrolyte replacement (chloride and potassium) prior to pyloromyotomy
Administer thickened formula feedings in small frequent volumes
Prepare the infant for an immediate barium enema reduction

parameter_options.text: Serum electrolytes, acid-base balance, and urine output
Daily weight and hydration status (fontanelles, mucous membranes)
Stool occult blood and bilirubin levels

rationales.correct: Non-bilious projectile vomiting in a hungry 3-week-old male with an RUQ olive mass and hypochloremic, hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis confirms hypertrophic pyloric stenosis. Surgical pyloromyotomy is deferred until IV fluids and electrolytes are corrected (A1, A2) to prevent intraoperative respiratory depression from alkalosis.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies pyloric stenosis and prioritizes preoperative fluid/electrolyte stabilization.

patient_profile.history: Taking sertraline 100 mg daily; prescribed linezolid 600 mg IV twice daily for MRSA bacteremia

assessment.neurological: Agitation, confusion, diaphoresis, ocular clonus, inducible ankle clonus, hyperreflexia (4+)

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie diagram for this adverse drug interaction.

action_options.text: Discontinue both sertraline and linezolid immediately and notify the provider
Initiate cooling measures, IV fluids, and prepare to administer benzodiazepines and cyproheptadine
Administer dantrolene sodium and bromocriptine
Apply physical restraints to control neuromuscular clonus

parameter_options.text: Core body temperature and neuromuscular clonus/reflexes
Blood pressure, heart rate, and creatine kinase
Serum lithium level

rationales.correct: Linezolid is a weak reversible MAOI; combining it with an SSRI (sertraline) precipitates serotonin syndrome, distinguished from NMS by neuromuscular hyperactivity (clonus, hyperreflexia, tremor) rather than lead-pipe rigidity. Stopping all serotonergic agents (A1) and providing cooling, benzodiazepines, and serotonin antagonist cyproheptadine (A2) is required.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies SSRI + linezolid serotonin syndrome via clonus/hyperreflexia and initiates reversal.

patient_profile.history: Multiple prior abdominal surgeries; presents with 24 hours of crampy abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, and obstipation

assessment.gastrointestinal: Distended tympanic abdomen, high-pitched tinkling bowel sounds proximal to obstruction

diagnostic_results.findings: Dilated loops of small bowel with multiple air-fluid levels

questions.stem: Complete the Bow-Tie diagram for this gastrointestinal condition.

action_options.text: Maintain strict NPO status and insert a nasogastric tube connected to low intermittent suction
Initiate isotonic IV fluid resuscitation and electrolyte replacement
Administer oral polyethylene glycol laxative to clear the bowel
Administer an opioid-anticholinergic antidiarrheal

parameter_options.text: Abdominal girth, bowel sounds, and signs of bowel strangulation (fever, rebound tenderness)
Nasogastric tube output, urine output, and serum electrolytes
Serum thyroid-stimulating hormone

rationales.correct: Prior abdominal surgeries causing adhesions are the top cause of mechanical small bowel obstruction (bilious vomiting, high-pitched bowel sounds, air-fluid levels). NPO status with NG decompression (A1) and IV fluid/electrolyte repletion (A2) prevent perforation and hypovolemic shock while monitoring for strangulation (P1) and fluid balance (P2).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Formulates decompression and fluid/electrolyte management for mechanical small bowel obstruction.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with large left middle cerebral artery ischemic stroke

questions.stem: Analyze the patient's serial neurological and vital sign trend over 4 hours. Which complication do these progressive changes indicate?

assessment.neuro: GCS 11, lethargic, left pupil 4 mm sluggish

options.text: Cushing triad indicating severely increased intracranial pressure and impending uncal herniation
Hypovolemic shock secondary to osmotic diuresis
Expected permissive hypertension maintaining cerebral perfusion
Acute alcohol withdrawal delirium

rationales.correct: The progression demonstrates Cushing triad—widening pulse pressure/systolic hypertension (146/84 -> 198/78 mmHg), bradycardia (78 -> 46 bpm), and irregular bradypnea (16 -> 10/min)—alongside declining GCS and ipsilateral fixed dilated pupil (CN III compression), signaling critical cerebral edema and impending uncal herniation.

incorrect.rationale: Hypovolemic shock presents with narrow pulse pressure and tachycardia.
Permissive hypertension does not cause bradycardia, irregular respirations, or fixed dilated pupils.
Alcohol withdrawal presents with tachycardia, agitation, and tremors.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes progressive Cushing triad and CN III palsy across serial assessments.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with bleeding duodenal ulcer treated endoscopically 6 hours ago

questions.stem: Review the serial hemodynamic trend. Which interpretation best explains the patient's progression from 1400 to 1600?

assessment.skin: Cool extremities, anxious, urine output 30 mL/hr
Pale, diaphoretic, melena passed, urine output 18 mL/hr

options.text: Compensated Class II hemorrhagic shock due to active recurrent upper GI bleeding
Hemodynamic stability confirmed by systolic blood pressure remaining above 110 mmHg
Acute cardiogenic shock secondary to fluid overload
Vasovagal response to passing a stool

rationales.correct: Rising heart rate (82 -> 128 bpm), narrowing pulse pressure (46 -> 26 mmHg due to catecholamine-mediated diastolic vasoconstriction), oliguria (50 -> 18 mL/hr), and diaphoresis indicate compensated Class II hemorrhagic shock from rebleeding. Hemoglobin remains deceptively near baseline (10.1 g/dL) during acute whole-blood loss prior to hemodilution.

incorrect.rationale: Systolic BP does not drop until >30% blood volume is lost; relying on SBP delays shock recognition.
Oliguria, narrow pulse pressure, and melena point to hypovolemia, not overload.
Vasovagal responses cause bradycardia, not sustained tachycardia of 128 bpm.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies early compensated hemorrhagic shock via narrowing pulse pressure and tachycardia despite unchanged hemoglobin.

patient_profile.history: Postpartum day 1 following cesarean section for arrest of descent after 24 hours of ruptured membranes

questions.stem: Evaluate the postpartum assessment trend. Which complication is developing?

assessment.uterus: Firm at umbilicus, lochia rubra moderate
Severe uterine tenderness, foul-smelling purulent lochia

options.text: Postpartum endometritis requiring broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics
Normal physiological postpartum uterine involution
Breast engorgement fever
Postpartum preeclampsia

rationales.correct: Cesarean delivery after prolonged rupture of membranes is the primary risk factor for endometritis, characterized by fever >38.0°C, tachycardia, uterine subinvolution/tenderness, and foul-smelling lochia, requiring broad-spectrum IV antibiotics (e.g., clindamycin plus gentamicin).

incorrect.rationale: Normal involution progresses with a firm descending fundus and non-foul lochia.
Engorgement causes low-grade transient temperature without uterine tenderness or foul lochia.
Preeclampsia presents with hypertension, not fever and purulent lochia.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies ascending postpartum endometritis from serial vital and lochial changes.

patient_profile.history: Receiving IV gentamicin and piperacillin-tazobactam for intra-abdominal abscess

questions.stem: Review the 3-day laboratory and output trend. Which conclusion is best supported by these data?

assessment.I_O: Urine output 310 mL/24 hr (granular casts on urinalysis)

options.text: Nephrotoxic intrinsic acute kidney injury (acute tubular necrosis) secondary to gentamicin
Prerenal azotemia caused by severe systemic hypotension
Postrenal obstruction from benign prostatic hyperplasia
Expected therapeutic diuresis during infection resolution

rationales.correct: Progressive oliguria (<400 mL/day), rising serum creatinine (1.0 -> 2.7 mg/dL), BUN:creatinine ratio ~12:1, and muddy brown granular casts during aminoglycoside (gentamicin) therapy in a normotensive patient indicate intrinsic acute tubular necrosis (nephrotoxicity).

incorrect.rationale: Blood pressure remained normal and BUN:creatinine ratio is <20:1, arguing against prerenal hypoperfusion.
Granular casts point to tubular epithelial necrosis rather than mechanical obstruction.
Urine output fell from 1,450 mL to 310 mL (oliguria), not diuresis.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies drug-induced acute tubular necrosis from declining urine output, rising creatinine, and urinalysis casts.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with diabetic ketoacidosis receiving continuous IV regular insulin and IV fluids

questions.stem: Based on the 4-hour DKA treatment trend, which provider order should the nurse anticipate next?

options.text: Add 5% dextrose (D5 0.45% NaCl) to the IV fluids while continuing the regular insulin infusion
Discontinue the IV regular insulin infusion immediately because blood glucose is below 250 mg/dL
Administer IV glucagon 1 mg to prevent rebound hypoglycemia
Double the regular insulin infusion rate to close the anion gap faster

rationales.correct: In DKA, blood glucose normalizes faster than ketosis/anion gap resolves. When blood glucose falls to 200-250 mg/dL while the anion gap remains elevated (16 mEq/L), dextrose (D5) must be added to IV fluids while continuing the insulin infusion so ketoacidosis clears without causing hypoglycemia or cerebral edema.

incorrect.rationale: Stopping IV insulin before the anion gap closes causes immediate rebound ketoacidosis.
Glucagon stimulates ketogenesis and worsens DKA.
Doubling insulin when glucose is 215 mg/dL will cause severe hypoglycemia.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Recognizes the threshold (BG ~200-250 mg/dL with open anion gap) to add dextrose to DKA fluid therapy.

patient_profile.history: Admitted with severe rotavirus gastroenteritis and dehydration

questions.stem: Review the toddler's serial assessment trend. Which interpretation is most accurate?

assessment.hydration: Sunken fontanelle, dry mucous membranes, capillary refill 4 sec, no tears
Lethargic, mottled extremities, capillary refill 5 sec, 0 mL urine
Unresponsive to voice, weak thready brachial pulse

options.text: Decompensated hypovolemic shock requiring immediate 20 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid bolus
Mild dehydration appropriate for oral rehydration therapy
Effective compensation requiring maintenance oral fluids only
Septic vasodilation requiring immediate IV nitroprusside

rationales.correct: Children maintain blood pressure through intense vasoconstriction and tachycardia until late stages; a sudden drop in BP (84/50 -> 68/38 mmHg) paired with lethargy, mottling, and 5-second capillary refill signals decompensated hypovolemic shock requiring immediate 20 mL/kg IV/IO isotonic crystalloid boluses.

incorrect.rationale: Hypotension and lethargy indicate severe (>10%) decompensated dehydration, not mild.
Oral fluids are contraindicated in an unresponsive, hypotensive child.
Vasodilators are lethal in hypovolemic shock.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Identifies the transition from compensated to decompensated hypovolemic shock in a toddler.

patient_profile.history: Unrepaired Tetralogy of Fallot awaiting surgical repair

assessment.cardiovascular: Sudden severe central cyanosis and inconsolable crying after venipuncture; systolic murmur barely audible

questions.stem: An infant with Tetralogy of Fallot develops an acute hypercyanotic ('tet') spell. Place the nurse's interventions in the correct priority order from first to last.

items.text: Place the infant in a knee-to-chest position and calm the infant
Administer 100% supplemental oxygen via blow-by or face mask
Administer prescribed IV morphine sulfate 0.1 mg/kg to reduce infundibular spasm and hyperpnea
Infuse prescribed isotonic crystalloid volume bolus (10-20 mL/kg) to improve right ventricular preload

interaction.instruction: Place the nursing actions in the correct order.

rationales.correct: During a hypercyanotic spell, right ventricular outflow tract spasm increases right-to-left shunting through the VSD. Immediate knee-to-chest positioning (I1) increases systemic vascular resistance, forcing blood back into the pulmonary artery. High-flow oxygen (I2) follows immediately, then IV morphine (I3) to relax infundibular spasm and calm hyperpnea, followed by IV volume expansion (I4).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Sequences physiological reversal of right-to-left shunting during an acute Tetralogy of Fallot hypercyanotic spell.

patient_profile.history: Postoperative laparoscopic appendectomy; nurse accidentally administers 10 mg IV morphine instead of ordered 4 mg IV morphine

assessment.respiratory: RR 10/min, drowsy but arousable to voice

questions.stem: Place the nurse's actions following discovery of this medication administration error in the correct sequential order.

items.text: Assess the patient's airway, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and level of consciousness
Notify the prescribing provider immediately and prepare naloxone at the bedside
Document objective clinical findings, provider notification, and interventions in the medical record
Complete an institutional quality-improvement incident/occurrence report without referencing it in the chart

interaction.instruction: Place the nursing actions in the correct order.

rationales.correct: Patient safety always comes first: assess physiological status (I1), notify the provider to obtain reversal/monitoring orders (I2), document factual clinical care in the medical record (I3), and file an internal incident report separately for quality improvement (I4).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Prioritizes patient rescue before provider notification, factual charting, and quality incident reporting.

patient_profile.history: Requires sterile wound dressing change for an infected surgical incision

questions.stem: Place the steps for doffing (removing) personal protective equipment (PPE) after caring for a patient on Contact and Droplet Precautions in the correct sequence to prevent self-contamination.

items.text: Remove gloves using glove-in-glove technique without touching the outside skin
Remove face shield or goggles by handling the headband or earpieces from the back
Untie and remove isolation gown by turning it inside out away from the body
Grasp the bottom and top ties/elastics of the surgical mask from behind and remove, then perform hand hygiene

interaction.instruction: Place the nursing actions in the correct order.

rationales.correct: CDC sequence for doffing PPE removes the most contaminated items first: gloves (I1), followed by eye protection/face shield (I2), then gown (I3), and finally the mask outside the room (I4), concluding with thorough hand hygiene.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Executes CDC-compliant PPE removal sequence to prevent pathogen self-inoculation.

patient_profile.history: G2P1 at 40 weeks gestation; fetal head has delivered, but anterior shoulder is impacted behind the maternal symphysis pubis ('turtle sign')

assessment.obstetric: Shoulder dystocia recognized during second stage of labor

questions.stem: Place the emergency nursing actions for shoulder dystocia in the correct priority sequence.

items.text: Call for immediate obstetric and neonatal resuscitation assistance and note the exact time of head delivery
Assist the patient into the McRoberts maneuver by hyperflexing her thighs sharply onto her abdomen
Apply firm downward suprapubic pressure just above the symphysis pubis (avoiding fundal pressure)
Assess the newborn immediately after delivery for clavicular fracture, brachial plexus palsy, and respiratory depression

interaction.instruction: Place the nursing actions in the correct order.

rationales.correct: In shoulder dystocia, calling for help and recording head-to-body delivery time (I1) comes first, followed by McRoberts maneuver (I2) to flatten the sacral promontory and rotate the symphysis pubis, then suprapubic pressure (I3—fundal pressure is strictly contraindicated as it worsens impaction), and post-delivery neonatal birth-injury assessment (I4).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Sequences McRoberts maneuver and suprapubic pressure safely during acute shoulder dystocia.

patient_profile.history: Scheduled for indwelling urinary catheter insertion prior to pelvic surgery

questions.stem: Place the steps for inserting an indwelling urinary catheter in a female patient in the correct sterile sequence.

items.text: Perform perineal hygiene with soap and water, open sterile kit, and don sterile gloves
Separate the labia minora with the non-dominant hand and cleanse the meatus front-to-back with antiseptic swabs
Insert the lubricated catheter 2 to 3 inches until urine flows, then advance an additional 1 to 2 inches
Inflate the retention balloon with the prefilled sterile water syringe and gently pull back until resistance is felt

interaction.instruction: Place the nursing actions in the correct order.

rationales.correct: Proper aseptic catheterization requires baseline perineal washing and sterile gloving (I1), maintaining non-dominant hand retraction while cleansing front-to-back (I2), advancing 1-2 inches beyond urine return so the balloon clears the urethra (I3), and inflating the balloon before securing (I4).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Sequences sterile female catheterization steps to prevent CAUTI and urethral trauma.

patient_profile.history: Collapse in hospital corridor; unresponsive and pulseless

assessment.cardiovascular: Unresponsive, no carotid pulse, agonal gasps; cardiac monitor shows coarse ventricular fibrillation

questions.stem: Place the ACLS resuscitation steps for witnessed coarse ventricular fibrillation cardiac arrest in the correct priority sequence.

items.text: Activate the emergency response system and immediately begin high-quality chest compressions (100-120/min)
Apply defibrillator pads, verify ventricular fibrillation, clear all personnel, and deliver an unsynchronized shock
Resume chest compressions immediately for 2 minutes before performing a rhythm or pulse check
Administer epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO after the second shock, followed by amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO if refractory

interaction.instruction: Place the nursing actions in the correct order.

rationales.correct: In witnessed VF arrest, immediate CPR (I1) and early unsynchronized defibrillation (I2) are the primary determinants of survival, followed immediately by 2 minutes of uninterrupted compressions (I3), and vasoactive/antiarrhythmic medications (epinephrine 1 mg every 3-5 min, then amiodarone 300 mg) for shock-refractory VF (I4).

clinical_judgment.explanation: Applies ACLS shockable cardiac arrest algorithm accurately.

patient_profile.history: Septic shock requiring vasopressor support

provider_orders.instructions: Available concentration: Norepinephrine 4 mg in 250 mL D5W

questions.stem: A patient weighing 80 kg is prescribed a continuous IV infusion of norepinephrine at 0.15 mcg/kg/min. The pharmacy supplies norepinephrine 4 mg in 250 mL of D5W. At how many mL/hr should the nurse program the infusion pump? Round to the nearest tenth.

clinical_judgment.explanation: Accurately calculates weight-based continuous vasoactive infusion rate.
